title: Kneipp intervention for children in rehabilitation (KIKeR pilot) as a supplement to standard care for chronic respiratory diseases: feasibility and pilot study (WP1)
summary: The KIKeR-Pilot Study will investigate whether traditional Kneipp hydrotherapy treatments – can be a useful supplement to the medical treatment of children with chronic respiratory diseases such as asthma. Many children who come to a rehabilitation clinic suffer from recurring respiratory problems. Kneipp hydrotherapy could help strengthen their immune systems and improve their quality of life. The aim of the project is to develop a practical Kneipp program for pediatric rehabilitation and to test its feasibility, acceptance, and initial effectiveness. As a first step, interviews will be conducted with specialists, parents, and children to design the concept. The Kneipp intervention will then be tested in a pilot study at the Alpenklinik Santa Maria Oberjoch.

interventions.name: The first workpackage (WP1) is a non-interventional qualitative observational study in which no therapeutic measures are carried out.
